HomePage.heading: Hi, I'm Vladimir — a Full-Stack Developer passionate about modern web development
HomePage.description: I build scalable and maintainable web applications with a focus on clean architecture, modern technologies and intuitive user experiences.
HomePage.quote: The best code is not the one that is the most complex, but the one that is most understandable

frontend.javascript: I started my JavaScript journey in 2021 during the COVID period and have been continuously improving my skills ever since. Over the years, I’ve built a strong foundation through constant practice and real projects.
frontend.html5: I have solid knowledge of semantic HTML5 and building accessible, well-structured web pages. I completed my course with excellent results and learned from an outstanding lecturer.
frontend.css3: CSS3 has been one of the most challenging and rewarding parts of web development for me. I continuously improve my styling and layout skills through practice, courses, and learning from the community.
frontend.typescript: I enjoy working with TypeScript and writing type-safe, maintainable codebases. Modern libraries provide excellent type support, which makes development more reliable and scalable.
frontend.react: React is my favorite frontend technology and the tool I use most for modern web applications. I have built multiple projects using React and its modern ecosystem.

backend.typescript: Type safety helps me build more reliable and maintainable backend applications. I enjoy the structure and confidence TypeScript provides on the server side.
backend.nodejs: Node.js is one of my favorite technologies for building backend systems and application logic. I enjoy creating secure and scalable server-side applications with it.

databases.mongodb: MongoDB was the first database I learned and helped me start my backend journey. While it has its strengths, I now prefer working with SQL databases for most projects.
databases.postgresql: PostgreSQL is my preferred database today, especially when combined with Drizzle ORM. I appreciate its type safety, flexibility, and powerful relational features.

frameworks.nextjs: Next.js was a game changer for me in the React ecosystem and became my preferred framework. I have a strong understanding of its architecture, routing, and modern features.
frameworks.angular: Angular was challenging at first, but I enjoy learning complex technologies and growing through them. It has become one of the most interesting frameworks I’ve worked with.
frameworks.react-router: React Router is a newer technology in my stack that I started learning independently in 2026. My experience with other frameworks helped me quickly understand its concepts and patterns.
frameworks.expressjs: Express.js is the standard backend framework in the JavaScript ecosystem and I have been working with it since 2023. I have built several backend projects using Express and Node.js.

libraries.next-auth: NextAuth.js is a secure and reliable authentication library that I have used with Google, GitHub, and credentials providers. I have also implemented features such as email verification and password reset flows.
libraries.handlebars: Handlebars was one of the first templating engines I worked with while learning Express.js in 2023. It helped me understand server-side rendering and traditional web application architecture.
libraries.mongoose: Mongoose is a powerful ODM for MongoDB that provides schema validation and a cleaner development experience. Although it can be slower than the native driver, I prefer it for the safety and structure it adds.
libraries.drizzle-orm: Drizzle ORM has been a game changer for working with PostgreSQL and TypeScript. I really enjoy its type safety, SQL-like approach, and flexibility for complex queries.
libraries.tailwindcss: Tailwind CSS has become my standard approach for styling modern applications. I use it in most of my projects because its utility-first workflow makes development faster and cleaner.
libraries.shadcn-ui: shadcn/ui is currently my favorite component library because of its simplicity and customization freedom. Most of my recent projects are built using shadcn components.
libraries.material-ui: I have practical experience with Material UI from several past projects. While I now prefer shadcn/ui, Material UI helped me understand large-scale component-based design systems.
libraries.react-hook-form: React Hook Form makes working with forms fast, efficient, and scalable. Combined with Zod, it provides an excellent developer experience for validation and form management.
libraries.zod: Zod is one of my favorite validation tools for both frontend and backend applications. I use it in most of my projects to ensure type safety and reliable data validation.
libraries.next-intl: next-intl is a newer library in my stack that I started learning in 2026. I enjoy exploring internationalization and building multilingual applications with modern Next.js practices.

devops.devops: I have experience with DevOps practices and automation using GitHub and GitHub Actions. I enjoy improving development workflows and automating repetitive tasks.
devops.jenkins: I have worked with Jenkins for creating automated workflows for testing and deployment. It helped me better understand CI/CD pipelines and deployment automation.
devops.docker: I have experience working with Docker for building images and running applications in isolated environments. It helps simplify development and deployment workflows.
devops.containers: Containerization allows applications to run consistently across different machines and environments. I understand the benefits containers provide for scalability and reliability.
devops.azure: I have a general understanding of Azure from coursework completed in 2025, including deployment workflows and cloud service management.
devops.vercel: Vercel provides a fast and simple way to deploy modern web applications. I have used it to deploy and manage projects efficiently through its free hosting platform.

AboutMe.heading: Hello, my name is Vladimir!
paragraphs: I am a passionate full-stack web developer with experience in modern web development since 2021, combining formal education, continuous self-learning, and hands-on project development.

Over the years, I have worked on a wide range of personal projects, building applications independently from concept to deployment. Through this process, I have developed strong problem-solving skills, critical thinking, and the ability to adapt quickly when facing unfamiliar technologies or complex technical challenges.

I enjoy creating scalable and maintainable applications with a strong focus on clean architecture, readable code, performance, and user experience. I continuously improve my skills through advanced courses, technical books, documentation, and practical experimentation.

My development journey has included working with both frontend and backend technologies, authentication systems, relational databases, API integrations, and modern frameworks. I especially enjoy solving real-world problems through software and creating projects that have practical value.

I work well both independently and as part of a team, and I value communication, responsibility, and continuous improvement. I strive to follow best practices such as clean code principles, component reusability, maintainable architecture, and Test-Driven Development (TDD) whenever appropriate.

When it comes to frontend development, my favorite technology is React because of its flexibility, ecosystem, and developer experience. At the same time, I also enjoy working with Angular, as its structure and architecture challenge me to think differently and improve as a developer.
I am always motivated to learn new technologies while continuing to deepen my understanding of the tools and concepts I already use.
